method.label: Turn age multiples into divisor counts

annotationRationale: Fixed age differences turn qualifying birthdays into positive divisors. The divisor-count formula restricts the prime exponents and determines the ages.
sourceMethod: Follows the official age-ratio and divisor-count argument. Makes explicit that the requested future two-digit age supplies the bound used to select the age difference 36.

review.mathCheck: Qualifying birthdays correspond bijectively to positive divisors of \(n-1\). Nine divisors force \(n-1=p^8\) or \(p^2q^2\). The two-digit future age implies \(n-1<100\), leaving only 36. Joey is initially 38; divisors of 37 give the next qualifying birthday at age 74, with digit sum 11, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution 19 on pages 8–9. It explains the divisor-count formula and explicitly justifies the size restriction used by the official solution.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed divisor-count skill and supporting prime-factorization skill match the argument. No material omission.
